revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Making Concrete
revealWordProblem.text:
Michael's mother needs to set four posts for her garden fence. She uses the concrete mix shown, and each post takes 250 ounces of mix.
Question: How many bags of concrete mix and how many quarts of water will she need?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A bag of fast-setting concrete with mixing directions: 1 bag (60 lbs) of concrete mix with 1 and one-half gallons of water.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Four posts need 4 × 250 = 1,000 ounces of mix. One bag holds 60 pounds, and 60 × 16 = 960 ounces, so one bag is not enough — she needs 2 bags. Each bag takes 1½ gallons of water, so 2 bags take 3 gallons. There are 4 quarts in a gallon, so 3 × 4 = 12 quarts of water. She needs 2 bags of mix and 12 quarts of water.

questions.stem: There are 12 inches in 1 foot. How many inches are in 5 feet?
questions.explanation: Inches are smaller than feet, so multiply by the unit ratio: 5 × 12 = 60 inches.
choiceFeedback: That adds 5 + 12. Converting scales the amount, so multiply.
That subtracts 12 − 5. Converting is not a subtraction.
hints: Write the unit ratio first: 12 inches : 1 foot.
Inches are smaller, so the number gets bigger — multiply.
questions.stemEs: Hay 12 pulgadas en 1 pie. ¿Cuántas pulgadas hay en 5 pies?
questions.explanationEs: Las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que multiplica por la razón unitaria: 5 × 12 = 60 pulgadas.
hintsEs: Escribe primero la razón unitaria: 12 pulgadas : 1 pie.
Las pulgadas son más pequeñas, así que el número se hace mayor — multiplica.

questions.stem: There are 1,000 milliliters in 1 liter. How many milliliters are in 3 liters?
questions.explanation: Multiply by the unit ratio: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 milliliters.
choiceFeedback: That adds instead of multiplying.
30 is far too small — one liter alone is already 1,000 mL.
hints: The unit ratio is 1,000 mL : 1 L.
Milliliters are smaller, so multiply.
questions.stemEs: Hay 1,000 mililitros en 1 litro. ¿Cuántos mililitros hay en 3 litros?
questions.explanationEs: Multiplica por la razón unitaria: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 mililitros.
hintsEs: La razón unitaria es 1,000 mL : 1 L.
Los mililitros son más pequeños, así que multiplica.

questions.stem: There are 16 ounces in 1 pound. How many pounds is 48 ounces?
questions.explanation: Pounds are the LARGER unit, so divide: 48 ÷ 16 = 3 pounds.
choiceFeedback: That adds 48 + 16. Converting to a larger unit divides.
That multiplies. Multiplying goes to the smaller unit, not the larger one.
That subtracts 48 − 16.
hints: Which unit is larger, an ounce or a pound?
Converting to the larger unit takes fewer of them, so divide.
questions.stemEs: Hay 16 onzas en 1 libra. ¿Cuántas libras son 48 onzas?
questions.explanationEs: Las libras son la unidad MÁS GRANDE, así que divide: 48 ÷ 16 = 3 libras.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál unidad es más grande, una onza o una libra?
Convertir a la unidad más grande requiere menos de ellas, así que divide.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake when converting within a measurement system is choosing the operation by habit instead of by unit size — multiplying every time. Converting 36 inches to feet by multiplying gives 36 × 12 = 432 feet, taller than a 40-story building. Ask first which unit is smaller: it takes MORE small units to make the same amount, so going to a smaller unit multiplies, and going to a larger unit divides.

choices: Yes, because 4 feet = 48 inches, which is more than 44
You cannot compare feet and inches
level1.explanation: Convert first so both measurements use the same unit: 4 × 12 = 48 inches. 48 > 44, so the child can ride.
choiceFeedback: 4 feet and 44 inches use different units — comparing the bare numbers is what the conversion prevents.

hintsEs: No puedes comparar dos unidades distintas directamente.
Convierte los pies a pulgadas con la razón unitaria 12 : 1.
Luego compara 48 con 44.

level2.explanation: Convert first: 4 L = 4,000 mL. Then solve ? × 500 = 4,000, giving 8 fills.

2 × 500 = 1,000 mL, only one liter.
40 × 500 = 20,000 mL, which is 20 liters.
hints: Get both amounts into the same unit first.

level2.explanationEs: Convierte primero: 4 L = 4,000 mL. Luego resuelve ? × 500 = 4,000, lo que da 8 llenadas.
hintsEs: Pon primero las dos cantidades en la misma unidad.
4 litros son 4,000 mililitros.
¿Qué número por 500 es igual a 4,000?

level2.stem: Sort each conversion by what happens to the NUMBER.
level2.explanation: Going to a smaller unit takes more of them, so the number grows. Going to a larger unit takes fewer, so the number shrinks. The amount itself never changes.
hints: Ask which unit is smaller.
More small units are needed to make the same amount.
Smaller unit → bigger number.

choiceFeedback: That adds 2 + 12.

12 inches is only 1 foot.
hints: The unit ratio is 12 : 1.

hintsEs: La razón unitaria es 12 : 1.

level2.explanation: Liters are the larger unit, so divide: 2,000 ÷ 1,000 = 2 liters.

hintsEs: ¿Cuál unidad es más grande?

level2.explanation: Cups and quarts are both customary units of capacity. The other pairs each mix a customary unit with a metric one.

level2.stem: Michael's mother is setting four fence posts. Each post needs 250 ounces of concrete mix, one bag holds 80 ounces, and each bag needs 1 quart of water. How many bags and how many cups of water does she need? Show your conversions.
level2.sampleAnswer: Total mix: 4 posts × 250 ounces = 1,000 ounces. Bags needed: 1,000 ÷ 80 = 12.5, and you cannot buy half a bag, so she needs 13 bags. Water: each bag takes 1 quart, so 13 bags take 13 quarts. Converting to cups with the unit ratio 4 cups : 1 quart, 13 × 4 = 52 cups of water. The two conversions go opposite ways: ounces to bags divides (a bag is the larger unit), while quarts to cups multiplies (a cup is the smaller unit).
hints: Find the total ounces of mix first.
Divide by the ounces in one bag — then think about whether you can buy part of a bag.
Convert quarts to cups with the 4 : 1 unit ratio.
level2.stemEs: La mamá de Michael está colocando cuatro postes de cerca. Cada poste necesita 250 onzas de mezcla de concreto, una bolsa contiene 80 onzas, y cada bolsa necesita 1 cuarto de galón de agua. ¿Cuántas bolsas y cuántas tazas de agua necesita? Muestra tus conversiones.
hintsEs: Halla primero el total de onzas de mezcla.
Divide entre las onzas de una bolsa — y luego piensa si puedes comprar parte de una bolsa.
Convierte cuartos de galón a tazas con la razón unitaria 4 : 1.

level2.stem: Match each unit ratio to its conversion.
level2.explanation: Every unit ratio says how many of the smaller unit fit inside exactly 1 of the larger one.
hints: Read each ratio as 'this many small units per 1 big unit'.
Which unit has 1,000 tiny parts?
Which has 16?

hints: Metric units use prefixes like milli- and kilo-.

Liter, gram, milliliter are metric.

level3.stem: A tap fills 250 milliliters every 10 seconds. Will it fill a 3-liter jug in under 2 minutes?
choices: Yes — it delivers 3,000 mL in 120 seconds, exactly filling the jug at the 2-minute mark
No — 250 mL in 10 seconds is far too slow for 3 liters
Yes — 3 liters is only 300 mL, so it takes 12 seconds
There is not enough information to tell
level3.explanation: Two conversions, then a comparison. 3 liters = 3,000 mL, and 2 minutes = 120 seconds. At 250 mL per 10 seconds the tap delivers 25 mL per second, so 120 × 25 = 3,000 mL — it fills the jug exactly at 2 minutes, not under it.
choiceFeedback: Check the rate: 25 mL per second over 120 seconds is 3,000 mL, which is the whole jug.
3 liters is 3,000 mL, not 300 — that is off by a factor of ten.
Everything needed is here: a rate, a volume, and a time.
hints: Two different units are in play. Put the volumes in the same one first.
How many millilitres does the tap deliver in one second?
Multiply that per-second rate by 120 seconds and compare with 3,000.
level3.stemEs: Un grifo llena 250 mililitros cada 10 segundos. ¿Llenará una jarra de 3 litros en menos de 2 minutos?
choicesEs: Sí — entrega 3,000 mL en 120 segundos, llenando la jarra justo al llegar a los 2 minutos
No — 250 mL en 10 segundos es demasiado lento para 3 litros
Sí — 3 litros son solo 300 mL, así que tarda 12 segundos
No hay información suficiente para saberlo
level3.explanationEs: Dos conversiones y luego una comparación. 3 litros = 3,000 mL y 2 minutos = 120 segundos. A 250 mL cada 10 segundos el grifo entrega 25 mL por segundo, así que 120 × 25 = 3,000 mL — llena la jarra exactamente a los 2 minutos, no antes.
hintsEs: Hay dos unidades distintas. Primero escribe los volúmenes en la misma unidad.
¿Cuántos mililitros entrega el grifo en un segundo?
Multiplica esa tasa por segundo por 120 segundos y compárala con 3,000.

level3.stem: A shelf is 5 feet long. A row of books measures 58 inches. Which is longer, and by how much?
level3.explanation: Nothing here states the conversion — you supply it. 5 feet is 5 × 12 = 60 inches, and 60 − 58 = 2, so the shelf is longer by 2 inches and the books fit.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 58 − 5, comparing a number of inches with a number of feet.
The shelf is the longer one: 60 inches against 58.
60 and 58 are two inches apart.
hints: The stem does not give you the conversion. What is it?
Write the shelf in inches so both measurements share a unit.
Then subtract the smaller from the larger.
level3.stemEs: Un estante mide 5 pies de largo. Una fila de libros mide 58 pulgadas. ¿Cuál es más largo y por cuánto?
level3.explanationEs: Aquí nada te da la conversión — la aportas tú. 5 pies son 5 × 12 = 60 pulgadas, y 60 − 58 = 2, así que el estante es más largo por 2 pulgadas y los libros caben.
hintsEs: El enunciado no te da la conversión. ¿Cuál es?
Escribe el estante en pulgadas para que ambas medidas compartan una unidad.
Luego resta la menor de la mayor.

level3.stem: Claim: “Converting a measurement to a smaller unit always makes the number bigger.” Always, sometimes, or never true?
choices: Always — a smaller unit means more of them are needed to cover the same amount
Sometimes — it depends whether you multiply or divide
Never — converting cannot change the number
Sometimes — it is true for length but not for mass
level3.explanation: It is always true, and the reason is what matters: the measurement itself does not change, only the unit you count it in. Smaller units means more of them fit into the same quantity, so the count rises — 1 foot becomes 12 inches, 1 litre becomes 1,000 millilitres. The unit and the number move in opposite directions.
choiceFeedback: Which operation you use is decided BY the direction of the conversion — it is not a separate case.
The number does change; the quantity it describes does not.
It holds in every measurement system — length, mass and volume alike.
hints: Try it on one you know: 1 foot in inches, then 1 litre in millilitres.
Did the amount of stuff change, or only the unit counting it?
If each unit is smaller, do you need more of them or fewer?
level3.stemEs: Afirmación: “Convertir una medida a una unidad más pequeña siempre hace que el número sea mayor.” ¿Siempre, a veces o nunca es cierto?
choicesEs: Siempre — una unidad más pequeña significa que hacen falta más para cubrir la misma cantidad
A veces — depende de si multiplicas o divides
Nunca — convertir no puede cambiar el número
A veces — es cierto para la longitud pero no para la masa
level3.explanationEs: Siempre es cierto, y lo que importa es la razón: la medida en sí no cambia, solo cambia la unidad con la que la cuentas. Unidades más pequeñas significan que caben más en la misma cantidad, así que el conteo sube — 1 pie pasa a ser 12 pulgadas, 1 litro pasa a ser 1,000 mililitros. La unidad y el número se mueven en direcciones opuestas.
hintsEs: Pruébalo con una que ya conoces: 1 pie en pulgadas y luego 1 litro en mililitros.
¿Cambió la cantidad de material o solo la unidad que la cuenta?
Si cada unidad es más pequeña, ¿necesitas más o menos?

level3.stem: Rosa converts 48 ounces to pounds by dividing: 48 ÷ 16 = 3. Theo builds up instead: 16, 32, 48 — that is 3 pounds. Whose reasoning is sound?
choices: Both — dividing and building up the ratio answer the same question
Only Rosa — building up is guessing, not converting
Only Theo — you cannot divide when converting units
Neither — 48 ounces is not a whole number of pounds
level3.explanation: Both are correct, and seeing why is the point. Theo is skip-counting the unit ratio 16 ounces : 1 pound until he reaches 48, which is exactly what dividing by 16 does in one step. Rosa's method is faster for large numbers; Theo's shows the ratio doing the work.
choiceFeedback: Building up a ratio is a method, not a guess — it lands on the same answer every time.
Dividing by the unit ratio is the standard method, and it is sound.
48 ÷ 16 = 3 exactly, so it is a whole number of pounds.
hints: Work Theo's counting out loud: how many 16s did he say?
How many 16s are in 48? That is the same question Rosa asked.
If two methods reach the same number every time, what does that tell you?
level3.stemEs: Rosa convierte 48 onzas a libras dividiendo: 48 ÷ 16 = 3. Theo en cambio va sumando: 16, 32, 48 — son 3 libras. ¿El razonamiento de quién es válido?
choicesEs: De los dos — dividir y construir la razón responden la misma pregunta
Solo el de Rosa — ir sumando es adivinar, no convertir
Solo el de Theo — no se puede dividir al convertir unidades
De ninguno — 48 onzas no son un número entero de libras
level3.explanationEs: Los dos son correctos, y ver por qué es lo importante. Theo va contando de 16 en 16 con la razón unitaria 16 onzas : 1 libra hasta llegar a 48, que es exactamente lo que hace dividir entre 16 en un solo paso. El método de Rosa es más rápido con números grandes; el de Theo muestra la razón haciendo el trabajo.
hintsEs: Di el conteo de Theo en voz alta: ¿cuántos 16 dijo?
¿Cuántos 16 hay en 48? Esa es la misma pregunta que hizo Rosa.
Si dos métodos llegan al mismo número siempre, ¿qué te dice eso?
